BW_spine.prompt: A hand-drawn painted 2D animation seen from a fixed elevated three-quarter camera looking down at about 53 degrees, on a flat solid pure green (#00ff00) background that stays completely unchanged and empty for the whole clip - no ground, no scenery, no shadows, no smoke, no sparks, no glow on the background. Camera locked: no zoom, no pan, no drift. This image is the FIRST frame: a small glass flask lying on the ground at the centre. The whole picture stays in exactly four flat grey tones - near-black outline, dark grey, light grey, white - with hard painted edges: no colour, no gradients, no soft glow, no blur, like frames of hand-drawn animation. Motion: in the first instant the flask shatters - a bright white flash, a few short straight light streaks radiating out, and a thin pale oval ring expanding along the ground and fading within half a second. Dark burning oil spreads out from the flask over the ground into a foreshortened oval pool about two-thirds of the frame wide, reaching that size within half a second and then never growing, never shrinking, never moving. Short flames rise from the pool and boil - they rise, hook, split and merge, constantly changing shape at a lively flicker of about three flickers per second, never standing still and never repeating; the tallest flame is about a third of the pool's width; it never becomes a tall fire. The pool burns steadily for about three seconds. Then the flames get shorter and fewer and go out, and the pool darkens into a ragged burnt smudge with soft edges that stays completely still for the rest of the clip. No people, no other objects, no text.
